relationships.subject: Nav1.7-F1624S
relationships.evidence_quote: Patch-clamp analysis of Nav1.7-F1624S revealed depolarizing shifts in both steady-state fast inactivation (17.4 mV, p < .001) and slow inactivation (5.5 mV, p < .001), but no effect on channel activation was observed.

key_findings: Novel SCN9A F1624S mutation found in PEPD causes depolarizing shifts of fast and slow inactivation of Nav1.7 without affecting activation.
Four SCN9A mutations (I136V, P1308L, F1624S, A1632E) identified in EM/EM-like and PEPD patients.
